summary: Frontend-only verification of palm-rejection / 'Pen only' fix on the Expo web preview. (a) Static code review of /app/frontend/app/draw/[id].tsx confirmed the new wiring is in place: const isStylusRef = useRef<boolean>(true) declared just above the Pan gesture (line 414); pan.onTouchesDown((event, manager) => {...}) callback (lines 420-443) reads event.allTouches[0].toolType (1=finger, 2=stylus, 4=eraser) and event.pointerType ('touch' | 'stylus' | 'pen'), and calls manager.fail() when settings.palmRejection && isFinger; onBegin (445-448), onUpdate (462) and onEnd (478-484) each contain the guard `if (settings.palmRejection && !isStylusRef.current) { ... return; }`; the previous flaky (e as any).pointerType === 'touch' checks have been removed from the bodies of onBegin/onUpdate (the only pointerType reads remaining are inside onTouchesDown's local isFinger/isStylus helpers, as expected). (b) Smoke / regression checks on web preview all passed: FAB (fab-create-note) -> Handwriting / S Pen -> Start writing (hw-create) opens /draw/<uuid> with zero console pageerrors; the tool-pen-mode toggle is present in the left-docked toolbar and flips its label between 'Touch on' and 'Pen only' without errors; the draw-more kebab shows the new Page color / Page template / Page size / Toolbar position rows; the draw-menu-toolbar picker successfully moved the toolbar to Bottom and Right (verified visually). Switching to Top/Left mid-loop hit a Playwright timing issue with the kebab re-opening, but no app-side errors were observed and the picker UI rendered cleanly each time it was opened. Opening a text note (note/<id>) renders the OpenTabsStrip with back-btn, opentab-<id>, opentab-close-<id>, pin-btn and more-btn testIDs (Chrome-style tabs). (c) IMPORTANT: The Expo web preview always shows the 'Stylus / S Pen canvas — Open this note on Android or iOS in Expo Go to draw with full pressure-aware stylus support.' fallback, so the actual finger-vs-stylus rejection behaviour CANNOT be exercised in the browser. The fix MUST be re-verified on the user's physical Samsung S25 Ultra after a fresh native build before this bug can be considered closed.
action_items: USER MUST RE-VERIFY ON S25 ULTRA NATIVE BUILD: The web preview cannot exercise Android MotionEvent toolType (1=finger, 2=stylus). Ask the user to rebuild and physically try writing with a finger while 'Pen only' is active. If finger drawing still happens, capture a logcat trace of the touch event and inspect event.allTouches[0].toolType in onTouchesDown — on a few OEM/keyboard combos toolType can come back as 0 (UNKNOWN) which the current isFinger check (toolType === 1) would miss.

Optional hardening: if user reports finger still drawing on S25 Ultra, extend the isFinger check to also treat toolType === 0 (UNKNOWN) as finger when settings.palmRejection is true, OR fall back to event.allTouches[0].size / majorRadius heuristics (fingers report size > 0.05, stylus ~0).
Optional hardening: add a one-shot Toast / haptic when palm rejection blocks a touch so the user has on-device confirmation that the guard fired.
critical_code_review_comments: draw/[id].tsx is now 1990 lines — well past the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting the Pan gesture + tool state into a custom hook (e.g. useDrawingGesture.ts) and the kebab/picker modals into separate components in a follow-up.

isStylusRef defaults to true, which is correct (fail-open for stylus on devices that don't report toolType), but it is module-scoped to the gesture closure only — fine for now. If multitouch handling is added later (maxPointers > 1) the ref will need to be keyed per touch identifier.

The onTouchesDown callback reads (event as any).pointerType — RN Gesture Handler's TouchData type does not formally expose pointerType on every platform, so the cast is necessary but it would be safer to type it locally as a discriminated union to avoid silent regressions.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Palm rejection fix lives in /app/frontend/app/draw/[id].tsx lines 414-494. The web preview renders a 'Stylus / S Pen canvas' fallback (no real gesture handler binding), so any future regression of this bug MUST be reproduced on a physical Android device — do NOT try to reproduce the finger-drawing bug in Playwright. Web-side regression should focus on: tool-pen-mode label toggle, draw-more kebab rows (Page color/template/size/Toolbar position), draw-menu-toolbar picker moving the toolbar to all 4 edges without console errors, and OpenTabsStrip rendering on /note/<id>.
rca_of_issue: Previous attempt only inspected (e as any).pointerType inside onBegin/onUpdate. On the S25 Ultra, Android's MotionEvent reports the tool type per-touch (toolType) rather than via the synthesized pointerType string, so the old guard silently treated finger touches as drawable. The new fix moves the decision into Pan.onTouchesDown (which fires before onBegin) and inspects event.allTouches[0].toolType (Android native field) AND event.pointerType (iOS/web), calls manager.fail() to abort the gesture before any stroke point is recorded, and additionally bails out of onBegin/onUpdate/onEnd via isStylusRef as a belt-and-suspenders measure. Reproduction in the browser is not possible because web Pan touches always carry pointerType='touch' regardless of input device, which is exactly why the old guard happened to behave correctly on web but failed on the device. Mitigation = native rebuild + finger test on S25 Ultra.
